Research-Project/LLM's/Adaptation-to-the.title: Adaptation to the Edge
Research-Project/LLM's/Adaptation-to-the.content:
Edge LLM
Several approaches can be used to make the models adapt to the edge environment, including the use of more compact models, quantification, pruning and distillation Zheng et al. (2025)
Compact models: A first approach consists of directly using models with fewer parameters. Small Language Models (SLM) thus seek to maintain comprehension and generation capabilities while reducing calculation and memory requirements, which facilitates their execution on platforms with limited resources
Quantification: Quantization consists of representing model parameters with a reduced number of bits, for example by moving from an FP16 representation to 8-bit or 4-bit formats. This reduction directly reduces the memory required for storing the model and the volume of data handled during inference, while performance gains depend on the ability of the engine and hardware to efficiently exploit the format in question. It also introduces a 11 numerical approximation whose impact depends on the model and the format used .
Pruning: Pruning consists ofremoving parameters or structures considered unimportant in order to reduce the size of the model and the amount of calculation necessary for its execution. It can be applied to individual weights or to entire network structures, such as certain attention heads or layers. The gains obtained at runtime, however, depend on the ability of the hardware and the engine to exploit the structure obtained 
Distillation:Distillation involvestraining a smaller model, called student, to reproduce the behavior of a larger model, called teacher. It thus makes it possible to obtain a model requiring less memory and calculation while seeking to retain part of the capabilities of the initial model

Research-Project/LLM's/Attention-Mechani.title: Attention Mechanism
Research-Project/LLM's/Attention-Mechani.content:
LLM Transformer
It originates from the attention is all you need paper by Vaswani et al 2017.
The attention mechanism allows the model to relate the different tokens in the sequence and determine which context information is most relevant to process a given token.

🟠Connects words and routes context across tokens .It uses cross tokens and accounts to 33% of the model,
🟢a query represents the information sought by a token( what do you offer), 🔴the keys make it possible to evaluate the relevance of other tokens in relation to this query, while 🔵the values ​​contain the information that will actually be combined.
“The Q \cdot K multiplication tells us how relevant token B is to token A (both in meaning and in relative distance via RoPE). Then, the attention weight acts as a volume slider on V, pulling in whichever specific slice of meaning that particular head’s W_v was trained to extract
Mathematically:
Matrix Q [N,1]
Matrix K [N,1]
Matrix V [N,1]
⇒ Q . K(transpose) →Matrix QK [N,N]
Attention = Q.K(transpose).V → matrix [N,1]

dk represents the dimension of the key vectors
M the causal mask which  prevents a token from taking into account the tokens located after it in the sequence
The QKT product provides scores representing the relationship between queries and keys
In the original Transformer architecture, several attention calculations, called attention heads, are performed in parallel according to the Multi-Head Attention (MHA) mechanism. Each head uses different q , k , v matrices that compute different aspects of context. ( for example , type of words : nouns , verbs. subject verb agreements , classifications etc…)
Variations:
Sliding window attention a variation in LLM and Decoder only models.
Group-Query attention
Flash attention

Transformer

Classification ,  is this token noun or verb?

Research-Project/LLM's/Batching.title: Batching
Research-Project/LLM's/Batching.content:
LLM Scheduling
Grouping some of them within  the same group, is called batching. The way in which this group is constituted and evolves during execution then depends on the batching strategy used .
Three main strategies :
Static: It uses a fixed number of requests per group which is unchanged until all queries have completed. This approach can introduce a wait before the start of the inference since it is first necessary to form a complete group and a wait at the end of the inference when the output lengths differ: a short query can finish its generation well before the others, while the group remains busy until the longest query finishes.

Dynamic batching: Dynamic batching, presented in seeks in particular to reduce the waiting time necessary to form a complete group. Instead of systematically waiting for a fixed number of requests, they are grouped for a short period of time and execution begins when the maximum group size is reached or when this timeout expires. The batch size can therefore vary depending on the available requests. Once execution begins, however, its composition remains fixed, so that short queries remain constrained by those whose generation takes longer
Continuous batching:  on the contrary allows the composition of the group to evolve during generation. It is based on scheduling on the scale of iterations where at each iteration of decode, completed requests can leave the group and be replaced by new pending requests, without waiting for the termination of other sequences . Continuous batching is now widely adopted in LLM inference systems and is a common mechanism to improve resource utilization when processing concurrent queries .

When this capacity is reached,additional requests remain pending. As resources become free, the system must then determine which ones to admit into the active batch, according to a scheduling policy that can be based on different criteria
Sarathi-Serve
Scheduling Policy

Research-Project/LLM's/Decode-Phase.title: Decode Phase
Research-Project/LLM's/Decode-Phase.content:
LLM Inference
Preceeded by the Prefill Phase

The inference continues with the decode phase. At each iteration, the last token generated is processed by the different layers of model  in order to produce a single new token, taking into account the context accumulated until then . Unlike Prefill Phase, the parallelism available within a query is lower, since each new token depends on the previous one.
The model parameters and information associated with the context must also be consulted at each generation step. The decode is therefore generally more constrained by memory accesses, in particular because this data must be reread at each iteration . A longer output thus implies more decode iterations and therefore more repeated access to the data necessary for generation Park et al. 2026

3- Second self attention mechanism Attention Mechanism:

query from decoder and key & value from the encoder.

Research-Project/LLM's/Feed-Forward-Netw.title: Feed Forward Network
Research-Project/LLM's/Feed-Forward-Netw.content:
LLM Transformer Encoder Decoder
The output of the Attention Mechanism is then processed by a Feed-Forward Network (Feed-Forward Network (FFN)).
In its general form, this is applied independently to the representation of each token and is based on several linear transformations associated with a non-linear activation function.
A first transformation generally projects the representation into a higher dimensional space before it is returned to its initial dimension.
The 🟢FFN thus makes it possible to transform and enrich the representations produced by the attention mechanism
Vaswani et al 2017
🟢It Refines each word individually and stores factual knowledge . It analysis each token by itself and account for 66% of the model

Research-Project/LLM's/Flash-attention.title: Flash attention
Research-Project/LLM's/Flash-attention.content:
LLM Multi-Head-Attention  GPU-Kernel Memory-management
Flash attention is a way to compute the Attention Mechanismfaster by minimizing the reads and writes from the GPU global memory to the shared memory.

Usually the global memory is big and slow and the shared memory is fast and small.
In normal attention , we first import the q , k  to shared to compute their result which is in [N.N] size then we write it back to global memory .Then we do the softmax to it which required recopying data from global to shared. Then we multiply by → recopying.
In Flash attention we only copy the values once in the sense that we compute the output gradually from the imported tiles of q , k , v while applying the softmax iteratively resulting in an output with less copying between shared and global memory.

q1 is fixed in shared memory while Ki , Vi are copied iteratively and in the same time the output is iteratively computed by the first picture.(fa2).
This result in a faster computation by drastically decreasing the memory copying.
There fa1 which basically flips the loops and makes kv outer and q inner so we had to compute o1,o2 …On and write them back but this is solved in fa2 by keeping q1 and looping over kn,vn to write o1 once.
Fa3 optimizes it based on the hopper nvidia series
fa4 optimizes it based on the blackwell nvidia series.

Research-Project/LLM's/Fragmentation.title: Fragmentation
Research-Project/LLM's/Fragmentation.content:
LLM Memory-management 
Internal fragmentation: part of the area reserved for a request remains unused when its sequence ends before reaching the maximum expected size.
External fragmentation: when queries of different sizes complete their execution, the freed areas can be dispersed into several non-contiguous spaces. The total amount of free memory may then be sufficient for a new query without a sufficiently large contiguous area being available.

Research-Project/LLM's/KV-Cache.title: KV Cache
Research-Project/LLM's/KV-Cache.content:
LLM Memory-management
During autoregressive generation, recalculating at each iteration the keys and values ​​corresponding to all the previous tokens would result in many redundant calculations.
To avoid these recalculations, inference systems use a Key-Value cache, or KV cache.
During Prefill Phase, the K keys and V values ​​produced for the prompt tokens are kept in memory.
At each Decode Phase iteration, only those corresponding to the new token are calculated and then added to the cache, while information relating to previous tokens can be directly reused when calculating attention . This reuse reduces the calculation volume necessary during decoding, at the cost of additional memory usage. The cache must also be consulted at each generation step. Its size increases with the length of the context and also depends on the architecture as well as the digital format used to store keys and values ​​. In a multi-user environment, multiple caches must be maintained simultaneously, which increases memory requirements and can limit the number of active queries 
Park et al. 2026
Kwon et al. 2023

Research-Project/LLM's/Memory-Management.title: Memory Management
Research-Project/LLM's/Memory-Management.content:
LLM Memory-management
As presented previously, the KV Cache of a request gradually increases with the number of tokens in its context. After Prefill Phase, it contains the information associated with the prompt tokens, then it grows by one token with each Decode Phaseiteration. As the final length of the response is not known in advance, the final size of the KV Cacheof a request cannot therefore be determined precisely at the start of its execution .
In a Multi-user inference, several KV Cache evolve simultaneously and independently. A classic approach consists of reserving for each request a contiguous memory area large enough to contain its cache up to a maximum length. This allocation simplifies memory management, but can result in two forms of Fragmentation

Research-Project/LLM's/MoE.title: MoE
Research-Project/LLM's/MoE.content:
LLM Feed-Forward-Network
Mixture of Experts:

Relating each token to the correct expert to use and to what extent.
Dense MoE:
Output is weighted average of all experts. Each expert contributes to a certain part of the output.

Sparse MoE (Used in LLM):
Output is weighted average of selected expert outputs and ignores all the others( Top K experts where K is chosen by us)

Routing collapse: Sometimes this causes certain experts to be consulted more than others which leaves them untrained and under tuned. Therefore , we force others to be part of the consultation via auxiliary loss.
Recent Trends:
We have also shared experts which minimizes redundant information between experts

Fine grained: Increase number of experts which makes each one more experienced in a special field.

Research-Project/LLM's/Multi-user-infere.title: Multi-user inference
Research-Project/LLM's/Multi-user-infere.content:
LLM
Since during generation only one token is made  at a time this motivates to exploit parallelism and run multiple queries to exploit and utilize the gpu fully Kwon et al. 2023. It is therefore necessary to organize their execution while taking into account the available resources  since queries order cannot be predicted. In this work, we are mainly interested in two aspects of this management:query scheduling(Batching
Scheduling Policy) and Memory Management
but the number of requests that can be maintained simultaneously remains constrained in particular by the memory necessary for their execution, which leads to the second aspect of multi-user processing: Memory Management

Research-Project/LLM's/Next-Token-Predic.title: Next Token Prediction
Research-Project/LLM's/Next-Token-Predic.content:
LLM Decoder
Idea 1: Take the highest predicted probability but this would result in a non optimum joint probability at the sequence end.

Idea 2: Beam Search , Keep the k paths that are most probable but this would also always result in same sequences and will thus lack creativity

These 2 will make the GPT and LLM sound robotic.
Idea 3: Sample the token from the probability distribution.
Top K: Sample among the top k most probable tokens.

Top P: Sample among the smallest set of token that satisfy a certain cumulative probability P

Research-Project/LLM's/Paged-Attention.title: Paged Attention
Research-Project/LLM's/Paged-Attention.content:
LLM Memory-management
PagedAttention offers KV Cache management inspired by virtual memory . Instead of reserving a large contiguous area for each request, the cache is divided into fixed-size blocks. From the query point of view,these blocks form a sequence of logical blocks, while they can be placed in non-contiguous physical blocks in memory . A block table maintains the correspondence between the logical blocks of a query and their physical location. Blocks are allocated gradually as the sequence lengthens and can be freed and then reused when a request completes. This organization thus avoids reserving a large contiguous area from the start for each sequence and greatly reduces memory fragmentation . This organization by blocks makes it possible to better use the available memory and to keep more requests active simultaneously . The scheduling and memory management presented in this section do not, however, constitute isolated mechanisms, since they are integrated into software dedicated to the execution of LLMs, called inference engines.
.A large part of these approaches has been developed for server environments with significant resources, while their use on Edge platforms imposes stronger constraints in computation, memory and energy, which requires specific adaptations presented in the following section .
These block can be shared in case they are common between multiple queries saving a lot of calculations.
Solves the Fragmentation issue.
Kwon et al. 2023

Research-Project/LLM's/Position-Informat.title: Position Information
Research-Project/LLM's/Position-Informat.content:
LLM Tokenization
Add position embedding to each token to have an embedding with position semantics.
Learned Position-specific embedding: Vaswani et al 2017
Add a position specific embedding to the token , but it is learning based so if we train the model on smaller sequences then once we prompt longer ones we will have no embeddings for positions in that are longer than what we learned.
Hardcoded position-specific embedding: Vaswani et al 2017
using sin and cosine functions to add the position embeddings to each token in a sense where smaller indices have a more varying frequency than the larger indices resulting in a much higher embedding as the tokens are closer.
→drawback is that the position embedding is added to the token layer itself which is irrelevant for the Feed Forward Network
position are relative only in the Attention Mechanism.
Therefore , do a change on the level of the Attention Mechanism.
add a bias to the softmax
→ T5 bias: bias learned per head
→ ALiBi : Bias is linear , deterministic
Common method now:
RoPE: Rotary Position Embeddings

Do not add bias but rotate the q , k matrices by a certain matrix rotation.
This will allow us to have a relation between positions as we compute the qkv matrix result in Attention Mechanism

the resulting matrix between two position will capture the difference between them in the output.
In this case each token vector will be rotated by a factor of dmodel/2 times for each 2 pairs of indices in the matrix  per attention head.

Research-Project/LLM's/Prefill-Phase.title: Prefill Phase
Research-Project/LLM's/Prefill-Phase.content:
LLM Inference
The prefill phase corresponds to the processing of the initial context  , prompt, provided by the user.
All the tokens in the prompt are processed by the Transformer blocks in order to construct their representations and produce the information necessary for generating the first token Park et al. 2026.
As the prompt tokens are available from the start of the inference, the operations associated with them can be carried out in parallel.
The main matrix operations are thus applied to several tokens simultaneously, which promotes good exploitation of the available calculation units. The amount of calculation carried out during prefill, however, strongly depends on the length of the input context: when this increases, the calculation volume and the quantity of data handled also increase
proceeded by Decode Phase
Summary: Can be carried in parallel since all the prompt is available at start

Research-Project/LLM's/Process-of-the-in.title: Process of the inference
Research-Project/LLM's/Process-of-the-in.content:
LLM Inference
The model successively generates the tokens composing the response

using this formula the model calculates the probabilities of each token based on the token that precedes it.
During inference, the text provided by the user, called a prompt, constitutes the initial context. From this context, the model calculates a probability distribution over its vocabulary in order to select the next token. This is then added to the context and used with the previous tokens to generate the next one. This process is repeated until an end-of-sequence token is generated or until a generation limit is reached.
This dependence between tokens imposes a sequential nature on generation, since a new token can only be produced once the previous one is available . Although the generation is autoregressive, the processing of the initial context and the generation of subsequent tokens do not have the same execution characteristics.

The inference process is mainly broken down into two phases: the Prefill Phase, devoted to processing the input context and the generation of the first token, then the Decode Phase, during which the following tokens are generated successively Park et al. 2026.
These two phases have different calculation and memory characteristics and rely on the use of the KV Cache

Research-Project/LLM's/Radix-Attention.content:

Research-Project/LLM's/SLICE.title: SLICE
Research-Project/LLM's/SLICE.content:

Proposes to differentiate them according to their priority level in order to adapt the use of resources to their different constraints. Research-Project/LLM's/Sarathi-Serve.title: Sarathi-Serve
Research-Project/LLM's/Sarathi-Serve.content:
LLM Scheduling
A long Prefill Phase can mobilize resources for a significant period of time and delay the Decode Phase iterations of already active requests, which leads Sarathi-Serve
to cut the prefill into several smaller fragments, called chunks, in order to gradually integrate them into the generation iterations.

Research-Project/LLM's/Scaling-laws.title: Scaling laws
Research-Project/LLM's/Scaling-laws.content:
LLM
A paper found out that better performance is with bigger models and bigger data.
The bigger the model → the more token efficient it is.
This is subject to compute power:
FLOPs ( Floating-point operations): meant to measure the compute → the higher the FLOPs the more the compute.
FLOPS (Floating-point operations per second): Compute speed measuring the hardware power.
There is a sweet spot between model size and training data size and it found that most models where undertrained compared to their size.

Research-Project/LLM's/Scheduling-Policy.title: Scheduling Policy
Research-Project/LLM's/Scheduling-Policy.content:
LLM Scheduling
Order of arrival:
First-Come, First-Served (FCFS):This policy selects requests according to their order of arrival. It is simple to implement since it does not require any additional information on the queries. However,a long query arriving first can delay the shorter queries that follow it, a phenomenon called Head-of-Line blocking .
Processing time:
Shortest Job First (SJF):
Seeks to favor requests whose processing is the shortest in order to reduce their waiting time. Its application to LLMs is, however, difficult, because the length of the response is generally not known before its generation. Some work therefore seeks to estimate this length or its relative order in order to approach this type of ordering.
Priority of requests:
A priority can also be associated with each request in order to process those considered the most important first. This priority can for example reflect different service levels or different latency constraints. When several requests have the same priority, their order of arrival can be used to decide between them . Scheduling thus makes it possible to increase the work executed in parallel.

Research-Project/LLM's/Sliding-window-at.content:

Research-Project/LLM's/Tokenization.content:
LLM Transformer
A process where input text is cut by a tokenizer into units called tokens. Depending on the tokenization algo, 🟢a token can correspond to a word, part of a word or even a character. Each token is then converted into a 🟢digital representation called embedding.🟢Position information is also integrated to emphasize on the orderVaswani et al 2017

End of sequence:[ES]

Research-Project/Research-Papers-Summari.title: Summary of Lina's Paper
Research-Project/Research-Papers-Summari.content:
LLM Edge Inference Memory-management Scheduling
Lina 2025
==🟢LLM’s on the edge:
Pros: Better latency privacy and dependant from cloud
Cons: limited computing and memory resources.
LLM inference has been studied more on server rather than edge.
Edge research concentrates on 🟢model quantization,load or platform (Adaptation to the Edge.

Chapter 1 : LLM + inferences on edge
This chapter presented the main elements necessary to understand Process of the inference in a multi-user Edge context(Multi-user inference). The operation of the Prefill Phase and Decode Phase as well as the use of the KV Cache make it possible to understand the constraints that appear when several requests are processed simultaneously, particularly in terms of Scheduling Policy and Memory Management. On Edge, these constraints are reinforced by more limited computing and memory resources, which also leads to adapting models in order to reduce their execution cost. These elements make it possible to address the solutions proposed to improve Multi-user inference and its execution on Edge.


Chapter2:


Different solutions have been proposed to improve the ==execution of LLMs in a Multi-user inference context and on Edge platforms== Zheng et al. (2025). In parallel, characterization work has studied the influence of the workload, the engine or the platform on performance and resource utilization .
Systems and optimizations for LLM inference


Edge platforms: the more limited hardware capacities lead to favoring solutions adapted to these constraints  Some solutions favor a lightweight and portable implementation, while others adapt the execution to the targeted platform.

llama.cpp focuses on lightweight deployment and portability.
ollama simplifies deployment

==In a multi-user environment(Multi-user inference):== efficiently organize the execution of several queries(Scheduling Policy , Batching) and their sharing of resources


In a multi-user context. It introduces iteration-level scheduling to allow the ==composition of the batch(Batching) to evolve during generation== rather than remaining fixed until all requests are completed.


This granularity of scheduling(Scheduling Policy) makes it possible to better process requests whose lengths differ and constitutes one of the principles adopted by systems using continuous batching today.


This evolution of the scheduling does not eliminate the interactions between the prefill and decode phases when several requests progress simultaneously. so Sarathi-Serve solved this issue to. This organization makes it possible to limit decode interruptions while retaining enough parallel work to maintain high throughput, so as to improve the compromise between throughput and latency under concurrent load.


The increase in the number of active requests also increases memory requirements, particularly due to the accumulation of their KV Cache.


vLLM  addresses this problem through Paged Attention, which directs it towards loads comprising a large number of concurrent requests.   This work thus shows that the processing of concurrent requests can be improved at several complementary levels: Orca and Sarathi-Serve mainly act on the Scheduling Policy, while vLLMand SGLang  also seek to better exploit the Memory Management and the information already calculated. Not well researched on edge





==Server Tests on Multi-Tenant Environments:==

Ay et Demirdağ (2026) compare ollama and vLLM on an NVIDIA H100 GPU by gradually increasing the number of concurrent requests. Depending on the scenarios considered, vLLM achieves a throughput of 20 to 29 times higher and a P95 latency of 8 to 19 times lower than that of Ollama under strong competition. The authors also observe that vLLM remains stable up to 100 concurrent users in their campaign, while Ollama encounters an initial bottleneck around ten users.
Bomhold et al. (2026) also characterize vLLM under concurrency on multiple GPUs available in the cloud. On an NVIDIA L40S, their load comprising 50 concurrent requests reaches around 2687 tokens/s, compared to 104 tokens/s in sequential execution. Their study also shows that the characteristics of the requests remain determining:increasing the output length mainly acts on latency, while lengthening the prompt more affects the time until the first token (Time To First Token, TTFT) .
Ye et al. (2025) finally show that, under competition, performance depends jointly on batching, query characteristics and the use of the KV cache on server GPUs or in cloud environments.

Edge Tests:

Dhar et al. (2024) highlight the hardware dependence by running an INT4-quantized LLaMA-2 7B model with llama.cpp on multiple devices The throughput goes from 0.11 token/s on a Raspberry Pi 4 with 8 GB of memory to 4.49 tokens/s on an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin  .Their analysis also shows that the limiting resource can change depending on the platform, particularly when the memory capacity becomes insufficient.
Arya et al  study the effect of several parameters on NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin, including sequence length, batch size and quantification Adaptation to the Edge. They observe that lengthening sequences reduces throughput and that a reduction in precision does not systematically lead to an acceleration, some of the smallest models studied can on the contrary be slowed down.
Laskaridis et al. [14] and Abstreiter et al. [1] also study the trade-offs between performance, memory and energy during local inference on different hardware and models.
Giedra et al. [10] evaluate twelve models ranging from less than one billion to around eight billion parameters on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Super. In particular, they obtain a median throughput of 18.13 tokens/s with GPU acceleration compared to 7.12 tokens/s in CPU execution alone. This work confirms that the model, execution mode and platform capabilities directly influence the performance obtained on Edge.
Park et al. 2026 come closer to a context combining Edge and competition. The authors evaluate 21 engines on multiple platforms, ranging from server infrastructures to an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin, while varying input and output lengths as well as the level of concurrency. Their campaign shows that the relative performance of motors depends on the load and the platform considered. However, it also highlights a difficulty in this comparison: not all of the engines studied can be deployed on all equipment. In particular, the authors are unable to run vLLM on the Jetson AGX Orin of their campaign, so that the comparison carried out on Edge does not cover the same engines as that carried out on server infrastructures.

The guidelines we are going to follow in the project:
